resources.string: Tempo writes every time this way: on Today, on the agenda and on the widgets.
In the words and the order of the app’s language.
Today is always on top. The days after tomorrow are listed briefly, so a week stays easy to read.
Holidays, birthdays and trips, in a row above the day’s events.
Invitations you said no to. They never take your free time.
Beside the clock on Today, when an alarm is set on the phone.
At the top of Today, beside the settings: opens your calendar app at today. A touch on the date does the same.

resources.string: There is no calendar on this phone yet. One added in your calendar app, or with an account, appears here.
Paper is warm white and amber. Vivid is cool white and azure. The same two as Chiaro and Passo.
Google Sans and Inter come with the app, so they look the same on every phone. System takes the font your phone is set in.
The colors come from your wallpaper instead of the palette above.
No account, no ads, no tracking.

Tempo has no internet permission at all, so it cannot send your events anywhere. It reads your calendar and never writes it: creating and changing an event happen in your calendar app. Android’s own backup, if you turned it on, keeps a copy of Tempo’s settings in your Google account, encrypted with your screen lock; your events are your calendar’s, and travel with it.
